subproblem.title: The blow-ups η_{x,λ_j#}T satisfy the hypotheses of the compactness argument
subproblem.statement: Let m, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, P := n + k, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)) with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N, x ∈ spt T ∖ spt ∂T (x ∈ T.support \ boundarySupport T), θ ∈ ℝ with HasMassDensity T x θ, and λ_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ) with λ_j → 0. Write η_j := dilation x λ_j (η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x)), U_j := η_j(U), A_j := η_j(U ∩ N) and S_j := blowUp T x λ_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j). Then: (1) every U_j is open; (2) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (3) every S_j is minimizing in A_j; (4) spt S_j ⊆ A_j for every j; (5) for every R ∈ ℝ there is c ∈ [0, ∞) with M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ c for all large j; (6) for every R ∈ ℝ, for all large j, ∂S_j(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j) with tsupport β ⊆ B_R(0); (7) for every G > 0 there are maps π_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) such that, for all large j, π_j is C¹ on B_G(0), maps B_G(0) into A_j, is the identity on A_j ∩ B_G(0) and satisfies |π_j(y)| ≤ 2|y| for y ∈ B_G(0), and such that for every η > 0, for all large j, |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_G(0). (Here B_R(0) = ball 0 R, 'for all large j' means 'eventually in atTop'.)

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0.1–0.4, 0.6 and 3.2 of the parent proof (Simon 7.3.1, proof display (1), chapter-07.txt lines 329–337). Sibling used: local_retraction (RET). Inherited dependencies (resolved dependencies of the parent node): dtc_blowUp_scaling (BU) and dtc_vanish_off_support (V). SimonGMT facts: GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, restrictDomain_apply, boundary_affinePushforward and tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset (Chapter06/AffineCurrentPushforward.lean, CurrentLocalEquality.lean), zeroRegion and support (CurrentLocalEquality.lean). The hypotheses ℓ ≤ k and (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ of the parent are not needed here (local closedness of N near x is built into the proper charts used by RET), so they are not assumed.
Notation: n := m + 1, P := n + k, λ_j := lams j, η_j := dilation x λ_j, so η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x) and η_j⁻¹(z) = x + λ_jz. 'For all large j' means 'for all j ≥ some j₀'.
0. (Unfolding the blow-up.) η_j is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with η_j(ball(x, s)) = ball(0, s/λ_j), η_j(closedBall(x, s)) = closedBall(0, s/λ_j), η_j⁻¹(U_j) = U and η_j(A ∩ B) = η_j(A) ∩ η_j(B). By the definitions of blowUp, affinePushforward_apply and restrictDomain_apply, S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) for every test form ω in U_j, where η_j^#ω := affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P λ_j) (−λ_j⁻¹x) ω is a test form in U with tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset). Since the boundary commutes with affinePushforward (boundary_affinePushforward) and with restrictDomain (both are composition with d on test forms), ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j), again with tsupport(η_j^#β) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport β).
1. ((1)) U_j is the image of the open set U under the homeomorphism η_j, hence open.
2. (A good radius.) x ∈ spt T ⊆ U ∩ N, so x ∈ U and x ∈ N. Since n = m + 1, boundarySupport T = spt ∂T = U ∖ Z_∂ with Z_∂ := zeroRegion(∂T) open; x ∈ U and x ∉ spt ∂T give x ∈ Z_∂. Choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ U ∩ Z_∂.
3. ((2)) Let R ∈ ℝ. If R < 0, closedBall(0, R) = ∅. If R ≥ 0, then for every j with λ_jR ≤ 2r (all large j, as λ_j → 0), closedBall(0, R) ⊆ η_j(closedBall(x, λ_jR)) ⊆ η_j(U), because z = η_j(x + λ_jz).
4. ((3)) BU(3), applied with A := U ∩ N (U is open and n > 0) to IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N), gives IsMinimizingIn S_j (η_j(U ∩ N)) for every j.
5. ((4)) Let Z_T := zeroRegion(T), an open set with spt T = U ∖ Z_T. Let z ∈ U_j ∖ η_j(spt T). Then η_j⁻¹(z) ∈ U ∖ spt T = Z_T, so z ∈ η_j(Z_T), an open subset of U_j. Choose ε > 0 with closedBall(z, ε) ⊆ η_j(Z_T) and put W' := ball(z, ε/2): W' is open and its closure closedBall(z, ε/2) is compact and contained in U_j. If ω is a test form in U_j with tsupport ω ⊆ W', then tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(closedBall(z, ε/2)) ⊆ Z_T is disjoint from spt T, so S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) = 0 by V. Thus S_j vanishes on W', W' ⊆ zeroRegion(S_j) and z ∉ spt S_j. Hence spt S_j ⊆ η_j(spt T) ⊆ η_j(U ∩ N) = A_j.
6. ((5)) Let R ∈ ℝ. If R ≤ 0 then ball(0, R) = ∅; a form with tsupport ⊆ ∅ is 0, so the only admissible form for massOn ∅ is ω = 0 and S_j.massOn ∅ = ofReal(S_j(0)) = 0; take c := 0. Let R > 0. HasMassDensity T x θ gives θ ≥ 0 and F(s) := T.massOn(ball(x, s)) / (ω_n·ofReal(sⁿ)) → ofReal θ as s → 0⁺, where ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞) is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝⁿ. Since ofReal θ < ofReal(θ + 1), there is s₀ > 0 with F(s) < ofReal(θ + 1) for 0 < s < s₀; as ω_n·ofReal(sⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞) this gives T.massOn(ball(x, s)) ≤ ofReal(θ + 1)·ω_n·ofReal(sⁿ). For j with λ_jR < s₀ (all large j), BU(1) with W := ball(x, λ_jR), together with η_j(ball(x, λ_jR)) = ball(0, R), gives S_j.massOn(ball(0, R)) = ofReal(λ_j⁻ⁿ)·T.massOn(ball(x, λ_jR)) ≤ ofReal(λ_j⁻ⁿ)·ofReal(θ + 1)·ω_n·ofReal(λ_jⁿRⁿ) = ofReal(θ + 1)·ω_n·ofReal(Rⁿ) =: c < ∞.
7. ((6)) Let R ∈ ℝ and let j satisfy λ_jR < 2r (all large j; every j if R ≤ 0). If β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j) and tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, R), then by step 0 ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) and tsupport(η_j^#β) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(ball(0, R)) = ball(x, λ_jR) ⊆ ball(x, 2r) ⊆ Z_∂, which is disjoint from spt ∂T; so ∂T(η_j^#β) = 0 by V applied to ∂T.
8. ((7)) Apply RET to N (dimension d := n + ℓ) and x ∈ N: δ > 0 and π with RET(i)–(iv); π(x) = x by RET(iii). Let s₁ ∈ (0, δ] be given by RET(iv) for η = 1 (π is 2-Lipschitz on B_{s₁}(x)), and for η > 0 let s(η) ∈ (0, δ] be given by RET(iv). Let G > 0 and define π_j(z) := η_j(π(x + λ_jz)) = λ_j⁻¹(π(x + λ_jz) − x). Let j satisfy λ_jG < min(s₁, r) (all large j). Then:
 (a) z ↦ x + λ_jz maps ball(0, G) into ball(x, λ_jG) ⊆ B_δ(x), so π_j is C¹ on ball(0, G) (composition of affine maps with π, which is C¹ on B_δ(x)).
 (b) For z ∈ ball(0, G) put y := x + λ_jz ∈ B_{s₁}(x). Then π(y) ∈ N by RET(ii), and |π(y) − x| = |π(y) − π(x)| ≤ 2|y − x| = 2λ_j|z| < 2r, so π(y) ∈ ball(x, 2r) ⊆ U. Hence π(y) ∈ U ∩ N and π_j(z) = η_j(π(y)) ∈ A_j; moreover |π_j(z)| = λ_j⁻¹|π(y) − x| ≤ 2|z|.
 (c) If z ∈ A_j ∩ ball(0, G), then y' := x + λ_jz ∈ U ∩ N (z ∈ η_j(U ∩ N) and η_j is injective) and y' ∈ B_δ(x), so π(y') = y' by RET(iii) and π_j(z) = η_j(y') = z.
 (d) Given η > 0, for j with λ_jG < s(η) (all large j) and y, z ∈ ball(0, G), the points x + λ_jy and x + λ_jz lie in B_{s(η)}(x), so |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| = λ_j⁻¹|π(x + λ_jy) − π(x + λ_jz)| ≤ λ_j⁻¹(1 + η)λ_j|y − z| = (1 + η)|y − z|.
This proves (7) with πs := (π_j)_j, and the proof is complete. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold blowUp: S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) and ∂S_j(β) = ∂T(η_j^#β) with tsupport(η_j^#ω) ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport ω).
Choose r with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ U ∩ zeroRegion(∂T); then U_j ⊇ closedBall(0, R) and ∂S_j = 0 on B_R(0) once λ_jR < 2r.
Minimality and mass scaling come from dtc_blowUp_scaling; HasMassDensity bounds M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) by (θ+1)ω_nRⁿ eventually; the support inclusion uses vanish_off_support.
Rescale the retraction of local_retraction: π_j := η_j∘π∘η_j⁻¹ maps B_G(0) into η_j(U ∩ N), fixes it, satisfies |π_j(y)| ≤ 2|y| and is (1+η)-Lipschitz on B_G(0) for large j.

audit.reason: The proof establishes all seven clauses using affine pullback, the inherited scaling and support results, finite density, and local_retraction. The rescaled retractions land in U ∩ N as required. Omitting the parent's dimension inequality and closure hypothesis is justified.
